extraction.name: CommonsenseQA
extraction.description: A commonsense question answering dataset of 12,247 multiple-choice questions generated from ConceptNet using crowd workers, with five candidate answers per question.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor; Jonathan Herzig; Nicholas Lourie; Jonathan Berant
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were generated by extracting subgraphs from ConceptNet, asking Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to author three questions per subgraph, add two distractors per question, verify question quality, and optionally retrieving Google search snippets as textual context.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ConceptNet triplets were the primary raw source; Google search result snippets were additionally collected as textual context.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: ConceptNet triplets were filtered by relation type, concept length/language, and edit distance; triplets were grouped into question sets of one source concept with three target concepts sharing the same relation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset creation pipeline filtered ConceptNet triplets, selected English concepts up to four words, removed low edit-distance pairs, filtered out low-quality questions through verification, and retained only questions verified by at least one correct worker.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: AMT workers authored three questions per ConceptNet question set, each question containing the source concept and targeting one answer concept while excluding the other two; workers then added two distractors, and a separate disjoint worker group verified whether questions were answerable and selected the correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question was verified by two workers, and only questions with at least one correct verifier were kept; this filtered out 15% of questions. Worker qualification was also enforced by requiring at least 75% of authored questions to pass verification.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to facilitate future work in incorporating commonsense knowledge into natural language understanding systems.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes reporting bias in web text and discusses risks of annotation artifacts and distributional biases in commonsense datasets more generally.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset remains substantially easier for humans than current models; retrieved web snippets do not appear to provide much useful information; and performance can be affected by distractor design and split choice.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for commonsense question answering and for evaluating NLU models; the paper uses train/development/test splits with an 80/10/10 split and considers the random split the primary split.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We hope that this dataset facilitates future work in incorporating commonsense knowledge into NLU systems.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Because questions are generated freely by workers, they often require background knowledge that is trivial to humans but is seldom explicitly reported on the web due to reporting bias (Gordon and Van Durme, 2013)... Investigations of commonsense datasets, and of natural language datasets more generally, have revealed the difficulty in creating benchmarks that measure the understanding of a program rather than its ability to take advantage of distributional biases, and to model the annotation process

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We find that the best model is a pre-trained LM tuned for our task and obtains 55.9% accuracy, dozens of points lower than human accuracy... We observe that using snippets does not lead to high performance, hinting that they do not carry a lot of useful information... Lastly, all SANITY models that were trained on COMMONSENSE QA achieve very high performance (92% for BERT-LARGE), showing that selecting difficult distractors is crucial.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: To investigate question answering with prior knowledge, we present COMMONSENSE QA: a challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering... We split the data into a training/development/test set with an 80/10/10 split... Since the random split is harder, we consider it the primary split of COMMONSENSE QA.
